headline: 🔥 355 COMANCHE IS AT THE TOP OF A BUYER'S LIST — Amy G. filed her form at 11:24 last night: interested YES, both price fields blank, and in her own words her buyers "really like the property and have put it at the top of their list." She is the same agent who called you from inside the house, and the basement lights she reported are still unanswered.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 AMY G. OF ETHOS INTERNATIONAL FILED HER FEEDBACK AT 11:24 LAST NIGHT off Saturday's 1:00 PM tour: interested — YES, staged 3, and in her own words — "My buyers have just started looking. They really like the property and have put it at the top of their list." ⭐ SHE LEFT BOTH PRICE FIELDS BLANK, which makes this the FIFTH consecutive read since the 8/5 cut where nobody argued the number. ⭐ And she is the same agent who phoned from inside the house mid-showing — the channel is already open and warm.
hotSignals.action: Call her today, don't email — you have a live thread with her already. Three things: answer the basement lights concretely (still open from her call), ask what moves her buyers from top-of-list to an offer — timing, possession, closing costs — and ask what she'd change on staging, since she scored a 3 and is the only agent to score staging since the cut. ⏰ 'Just started looking' means they tour more houses this week.

listings.note: ✅ CORRECTION WORTH READING: the inspection-response letter was NOT sitting unsent — Gene sent it himself Saturday 9:54 AM. The document still in drafts is a DUPLICATE created six minutes later and is flagged for deletion, not aged as pending follow-up. Two separate reads called it 'unsent for 24 hours'; both were reading the copy. ⭐ THE SHAPE OF THE ASK IS THE STORY: they inspected seventy-one items, flagged sixty-eight at some level, and asked for exactly three. That is a reasonable buyer. ⭐ The response sent was two yeses and a hold — agree to the basement leak and a scoped HVAC service; on the roof, don't say no, say give us a few days and our own licensed roofer's report. The inspector wrote in the same section that he cannot determine the roof's age or remaining life. ⚠️ FHA, so the appraiser can raise the roof independently, and the concession room under the FHA cap is small — this gets solved with work, not a check. ✅ Sellers have acknowledged the roof-holdback approach. ⭐ Closing 10/23.

✅ STILL THE CLEANEST FILE ON THE BOARD ON PAPER — inspection ran 8/5 at noon, appraisal 8/7 at 9:00 AM, both on primary ShowingTime notices, and the closing invite matches stored state. AN INSPECTION AND AN APPRAISAL BOTH SPENT IS THE STRONGEST POSITION ANY DEAL HERE OCCUPIES. 🔴 AND YET THE SELLER HAS BEEN WAITING ON A RETURNED CALL SINCE TUESDAY — five days, mid-transaction, on the deal with the least to worry about. ⚠️ The payoff was reported as "forgotten" rather than ordered. ⚠️ The appraised value still has not come back at day ten. ⚠️ The buyer's agent asked for a specific co-op commission and nobody has ever answered — real money on an otherwise settled deal.

listings.note: ✅ THE DELIVERABLE WAS LOCATED FRIDAY — the 19-lot plat, exactly what the open buyer chip had been waiting on since he answered "Yes". 🔴 THE THING THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU IS THE HANDOFF, NOT THE COUNTY: the builder asked the septic perc question on 8/12, your operations manager researched and answered it completely, and that answer has sat on her board since Friday with nobody reading it back to him. Day four — the work was done, the delivery never happened. ⭐ THE PERC QUESTION IS PRICED, NOT BLOCKED: county records are in-person only, weekdays 8:00–3:30, per-record fee — nineteen lots is a four-figure errand. So the choice is three-way: pull all nineteen, narrow to the lots a buyer asks about, or ask the developer first, who almost certainly holds the perc results from platting. PERC DECIDES BUILDABILITY AND BUILDABILITY DECIDES PRICE PER LOT. 🔥 Six names off this ad now, while every other ad in the portfolio produced zero.

oweFeedback.when: 🔴 THREE ASKS AND TWENTY-SIX DAYS OF SILENCE — 7/21, 7/22 and 7/23, from the RealtySouth Inverness listing side after your 7/21 1:00 PM tour. ⭐ THIS IS THE ONE THAT COSTS SOMETHING REAL, and the cost is not the courtesy — it is that the honest written answer IS your counter on the largest number on your board, roughly $36K of GCI. The listing side has asked repeatedly to be moved forward; a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal. Twenty minutes of writing moves it. ⚠️ The appraisal figure your buyer cited as far under ask is single-sourced from him — do not quote it to the other side as an appraised value.

⏰ TWO FEEDBACK REQUESTS, 7/31 and 8/1, from the Keller Williams Hoover listing side. The listing has since gone from CONTINGENT to EXPIRED between the two notices, so the ask is stale — but a one-line courtesy reply costs nothing and this is a Lake Crest-subdivision agent you will meet again.
